author: श्रीराघवेन्द्रस्वामी
commentary: अन्यदेवताभजनस्याल्पफलत्वेऽपि तदेव कार्यं सुशकत्वात् । त्वद्भजनं तु दुर्बलैरशक्यं कर्तुं, तवातिमहिमत्वादित्यत आह ॥ पत्रमिति । अनिषिद्धपत्रादिकं यो मह्यं भक्त्या ददाति । प्रयतात्महः । "यम उपरमे" । प्रकर्षेणोपरतमनस्कस्य विषयविरक्तस्य भक्त्या समर्पितमश्नामि । भक्त्यैवाहं तुष्टो भवामि न द्रव्यादिनेति भावः ॥ ९.२६॥
translation:
He who offers to Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water, that devout offering of him whose mind is restrained, I accept. (26.)
V. A leaf &c: those leaves, flowers, &c., which are not prohibited to be used as offerings. Prayatatmanah: Prayata + atmanah (mind); Prayata: Pra + yam (to restrain) restrained from going to other objects, i.e., filled with renunciation and unattached to objects of sense. Hence the term is often used to mean the pure in soul, ‘of hollowed spirit.' The Lord means that devotion is what delights Him; but not the offerings of material stuff. A Sri Krishna concludes by saying, 'Since even a little greatly rejoices Me, if offered with devotion, do thou the same.'
